problem:
A wooden box of mass $20\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the wooden box's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after the descent began, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the wooden box is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=\frac{2}{25}\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Which differential equation best models the velocity? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g,$ and the only forces acting on the wooden box are the weight due to gravity and drag.

activity_context.topic_title: Falling Body Problems With Quadratic Drag
